papers.title: Giant Room-Temperature Magnetoelectric Coupling Effect in Nanocomposite Thin Films via Strain-Sensitive Polarization
papers.authors: Hao Li, Yali Yang, Shiqing Deng, Yajun Qi, Peng Wang, He Qi, Huifen Yu, Yuan Zhang, Yu Chen, Jiaou Wang, Jianghua Chen, Jiangyu Li, Junling Wang, Jun Chen
papers.abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroic composites, which combine ferroelectric and ferromagnetic phases, are pivotal for next-generation electronic devices. Conventional design strategies prioritize ferroelectric materials with large spontaneous polarization to achieve strong magnetoelectric coupling. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting approach that instead utilizes a material’s high strain sensitivity of polarization. The quantum paraelectric SrTiO3 is discovered as an ideal ferroelectric component due to its exceptionally high polarization response to strain, far exceeding that of classical ferroelectrics like BaTiO3 or PbTiO3. To demonstrate this concept, the desired SrTiO3-NiO nanocomposite films featuring ordered nanopillar array and atomically sharp vertical interfaces were fabricated. This nanostructure maximizes the interfacial contact area and ensures highly efficient strain transfer. The resulting composite exhibits a giant direct magnetoelectric coupling coefficient of 3200 mV/(cm·Oe) at room temperature, demonstrating a remarkably strong macroscopic magnetoelectric response compared with conventional 1-3 composite oxide multiferroic systems. Through a combination of atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy and first-principles calculations, we reveal the outstanding performance originates from the unique strain-sensitive polarization of SrTiO3, which can effectively trigger substantial polarization variations via magnetic field-induced strain transfer across coherent interface. This work redefines the design principle for high-performance magnetoelectric composites by emphasizing strain sensitivity over large polarization, opening a new pathway for developing ultra-sensitive sensors and multi-state, low-power memory devices.

SrTiO₃–NiO nanocomposite films implement this approach and exhibit a reported giant room-temperature magnetoelectric response.

papers.title: Imprinting Macroscopic Orbital Angular Momentum onto the Superconducting Higgs Mode Using a Terahertz Vortex Beam
papers.authors: Kotaro Tanaka, Daemo Kang, Naotaka Yoshikawa, Fumiya Sekiguchi, Hirotaka Terai, Takahiro Morimoto, Ryo Shimano
papers.abstract: Understanding how angular momentum is exchanged between different degrees of freedom has long been a subject of fundamental interest, as represented by the Einstein-de Haas effect in a ferromagnet, in which a change of rotational speed of the rigid body is induced by a change of magnetization. Here, we report the imprinting of orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light to a superconductor, a macroscopic quantum state of fermionic condensate, through the Higgs mode excitation by a terahertz (THz) vortex beam. By using spatiotemporally resolved THz-pump and THz-probe spectroscopy, we observe a rotating order parameter oscillation in which the phase structure of the vortex beam is imprinted onto the Higgs mode. Time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau analysis shows that the rotating Higgs mode carries a finite OAM. This work opens a pathway for imprinting OAM of light onto a superconductor and manipulating its order parameter.

papers.abstract: In the localized phase of the Anderson model on the Bethe lattice, the inverse participation ratio (IPR) approaches its asymptotic value as the imaginary regulator $η\to 0$ with an anomalous power law, $I_2(η) - I_2^\infty \propto η^{2β-1}$, where $β\in (1/2,1)$ is the tail exponent of the local density of states distribution. We derive it analytically in a "toy" non-linear $σ$-model on the hyperbolic superplane, which shares the exotic criticality of the Bethe-lattice Anderson transition. Matching the bulk solution of its cavity equation to a boundary layer set by the symmetry-breaking field $H$ gives a correction $\propto H^{2β-1}$, controlled by the subdominant root $1-β$ of the linearized equation; at criticality it becomes $\propto 1/|\ln H|$. Under a few natural assumptions the same mechanism operates in the Anderson model, where the correction is a zero mode of the $η=0$ cavity recursion, as we confirm numerically, also for finite-size corrections. Through a spectral identity and an exact sum rule, the same exponent fixes exactly the decay $ω^{-μ}$, with $μ= 2(1-β)$, of the correlation function of two eigenstates at energy distance $ω$, including its amplitude, as we confirm by exact diagonalization, population dynamics on the infinite lattice, and analytically in the toy model. A counting of Mott resonances between distant localized eigenstates explains this physically; on finite graphs, finite-size corrections reflect a deficit of doubly-peaked eigenstates. Finally, we derive the finite-size scaling of the IPR in the variable $(2β-1)\ln N$, which describes both finite-$η$ and finite-$N$ data. It yields a Kosterlitz-type renormalization-group flow of the running fractal dimension: finite fractal dimensions of localized states at accessible sizes are a logarithmic finite-size effect.
papers.physics_advance: It derives the anomalous IPR correction exponent from the LDOS tail exponent, connects it to eigenstate-correlation decay through a spectral sum rule, and identifies logarithmic finite-size effects that can mimic finite fractal dimensions in localized states.
papers.relevance_reason: The work develops and tests a detailed theoretical account of anomalous eigenstate and finite-size scaling in Anderson localization on the Bethe lattice.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究推导 Bethe 格点 Anderson 模型局域相中逆参与率的反常修正，并将其指数与本征态关联联系起来。研究还建立有限尺寸标度描述，并将局域态表观的有限分形维数解释为对数型有限尺寸效应。
papers.method_en: The authors derive the correction analytically in a solvable toy nonlinear σ-model on the hyperbolic superplane and match a cavity-equation bulk solution to a boundary layer. They test related predictions using exact diagonalization, population dynamics on the infinite lattice, numerical cavity recursion, spectral identities, and an exact sum rule.
papers.method_zh: 作者在双曲超平面上的可解玩具非线性 σ 模型中解析推导该修正，并将空腔方程的体区解与边界层匹配。研究通过精确对角化、无限格点上的群体动力学、数值空腔递推、谱恒等式和精确求和规则检验相关预测。
papers.result_en: For regulator η tending to zero, the localized-phase correction obeys I₂(η)−I₂∞ ∝ η^(2β−1), with β∈(1/2,1), while at criticality it becomes proportional to 1/|ln H|. The same exponent gives the eigenstate-correlation decay ω^(−μ), with μ=2(1−β), including its amplitude; the authors report agreement with numerical checks and derive finite-size scaling in (2β−1)ln N, interpreting finite fractal dimensions at accessible sizes as logarithmic effects.
papers.result_zh: 当调节参数 η 趋于零时，局域相中的修正满足 I₂(η)−I₂∞ ∝ η^(2β−1)，其中 β∈(1/2,1)；在临界点，该修正则与 1/|ln H| 成正比。同一指数还决定本征态关联按 ω^(−μ) 衰减，其中 μ=2(1−β)，且包括其振幅；作者报告了与数值检验的一致性，并推导了以 (2β−1)ln N 为变量的有限尺寸标度，将可达尺寸下的有限分形维数解释为对数效应。

papers.future_zh: 进一步考察不同有限尺寸及临近转变区域，可检验 Anderson 模型中的所提标度关系和预测的本征态关联定律。摘要报告了数值检验，但未描述实验验证。
papers.tier_reason_en: The paper combines an analytic mechanism, an exact relation for eigenstate correlations including the amplitude, and multiple numerical checks, with implications for interpreting localization and finite-size fractality; this supports a strong short-format theory assessment.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 该工作结合解析机制、包含振幅的本征态关联精确关系及多种数值检验，并影响对局域化和有限尺寸分形性的理解；这些特点支持较高水平的短篇理论研究评价。

papers.abstract: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method. MnSiN2 exhibits both Wannier-type excitons with N-p to Si-s transition character and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons with hole on N-p and electron on Mn-d orbital character.
papers.physics_advance: It identifies MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 as altermagnets with a symmetry-supported magnetic ground state, and predicts their altermagnetic band splittings, chiral magnon features, and distinct Wannier- and charge-transfer-type excitons.
papers.relevance_reason: The study presents a substantive theoretical investigation of magnetic ordering, altermagnetic band structure, magnons, and optical excitations in candidate magnetic materials.

papers.method_en: The study combines symmetry analysis with spin-polarized density-functional theory and quasiparticle self-consistent GW calculations to assess the magnetic structures and electronic bands. It also calculates spin-wave dispersions, estimates Néel temperatures using mean-field and random-phase approximations, and evaluates the optical dielectric function with the Bethe–Salpeter equation.
papers.method_zh: 研究结合对称性分析、自旋极化密度泛函理论和准粒子自洽 GW 计算，考察磁结构与电子能带。研究还计算自旋波色散，以平均场和随机相位近似估算 Néel 温度，并用 Bethe–Salpeter 方程求光学介电函数。
papers.result_en: The calculations identify Pna′2₁′ as the lowest-energy spin configuration, consistent with neutron diffraction, and analyze symmetry-allowed altermagnetic band splittings for three antiferromagnetic patterns. The work also reports spin-wave dispersions, chiral magnon splitting, and Néel-temperature estimates; for MnSiN₂, it finds Wannier-type N-p-to-Si-s excitons and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons involving N-p holes and Mn-d electrons.
papers.result_zh: 计算确定 Pna′2₁′ 为最低能自旋构型，与中子衍射结果一致，并分析了三种反铁磁排列中对称性允许的交错磁能带劈裂。研究还给出自旋波色散、手性磁振子劈裂和 Néel 温度估算；对于 MnSiN₂，计算发现具有 N-p 至 Si-s 跃迁特征的 Wannier 型激子，以及空穴位于 N-p、电子位于 Mn-d 轨道的电荷转移 Frenkel 型激子。

papers.future_zh: 对预测的磁有序和磁振子性质进行实验检验，并测量所报告的激子跃迁光学响应，可用于评估这些计算结果。摘要未报告此类实验。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work combines symmetry classification with several complementary calculations and makes specific predictions for magnetic and optical properties, but its scope is primarily a focused study of two compounds.

papers.authors: Camilla Polvara, William Witczak-Krempa

papers.abstract: The square-lattice transverse-field Ising model has exact zero-energy eigenstates at any field: products of singlets on alternate plaquette diagonals. A longitudinal field isolates them from a symmetry-protected degeneracy. The mechanism is that a site coupled equally to both ends of a singlet annihilates it. The result thus holds for any spin $s$, anisotropic exchange, a large class of bond disorder and certain three-spin terms. This mechanism decides which lattices host such states: two of the 11 Archimedean lattices (four at $s=1/2$), bcc and quasicrystals with spins on the edges. Singlet pumping cools any state into them.
papers.physics_advance: Equal coupling to both ends of a singlet annihilates it, producing exact zero-energy many-body states across broad classes of spin interactions, disorder, and lattices.
papers.relevance_reason: This develops a general mechanism for exact many-body scar states in quantum spin models and identifies lattice settings where they occur, making a substantial contribution to quantum magnetism.
papers.summary_zh: 本文以单态覆盖构造精确多体疤痕态，并指出该构造在不同自旋模型和晶格中成立的条件。
papers.method_en: The construction uses the fact that a site coupled equally to both ends of a singlet annihilates that singlet product; the authors extend this mechanism to anisotropic exchange, selected disorder and three-spin terms, and propose singlet pumping.
papers.method_zh: 该构造利用如下性质：若某格点与单态两端的耦合相等，该项作用会湮灭该单态乘积；作者将此机制推广至各向异性交换、特定无序和三自旋项，并提出单态泵浦方案。
papers.result_en: The square-lattice transverse-field Ising model has exact zero-energy states at any field formed by singlets on alternate plaquette diagonals, isolated by a longitudinal field from a symmetry-protected degeneracy; the mechanism also identifies host lattices including two of the 11 Archimedean lattices (four for s = 1/2), the bcc lattice, and quasicrystals with spins on edges.
papers.result_zh: 正方晶格横场 Ising 模型在任意横场下都具有由交替 plaquette 对角线上的单态组成的精确零能态，纵场可将其与受对称性保护的简并隔离；该机制还确定了可承载此类态的晶格，包括 11 种 Archimedean 晶格中的两种（s = 1/2 时为四种）、体心立方晶格，以及自旋位于边上的准晶。
papers.future_en: Testing whether singlet pumping cools states into these exact scar states, and checking their robustness under the stated disorder and interaction extensions, are direct follow-ups suggested by the construction.
papers.future_zh: 检验单态泵浦能否将系统冷却至这些精确疤痕态，并考察它们在文中所述无序及相互作用扩展下的稳健性，是该构造直接引出的后续工作。

papers.abstract: Crystal-field quenching usually suppresses orbital angular momentum and limits magnetic anisotropy in transition-metal oxides. Here we identify charge disproportionation as a route to giant magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the layered polar metal Sr$_3$Co$_2$O$_7$. First-principles calculations reveal an energy preference of 234.0 meV per cell for in-plane [110] magnetization over [001]. Charge disproportionation and the associated polar displacement reconstruct the local cobalt crystal fields, creating inequivalent sites with distinct orbital hierarchies. This reconstruction enables a strongly directional orbital response, particularly at the displaced cobalt site, where orbital angular momentum is recovered for in-plane magnetization. Spin--orbit coupling converts this response into a large magnetic anisotropic energy. In the centrosymmetric reference, the orbital moments remain nearly quenched and the anisotropy is strongly reduced. A local Green-function and orbital-moment analysis connects the large energy scale to orbital unquenching, while the conventional second-order contribution is small within the adopted approximation. These results identify charge-disproportionation-driven orbital reconstruction as a design principle for large anisotropy and motivate layered perovskites and magnetic polar metals as platforms in the search for rare-earth-free permanent magnets.
papers.physics_advance: Charge disproportionation and polar displacement reconstruct cobalt crystal fields, unquench orbital angular momentum, and generate giant in-plane magnetic anisotropy.
papers.relevance_reason: The calculations identify a magnetic and orbital mechanism for exceptionally large anisotropy in a polar transition-metal oxide.
papers.summary_zh: 作者提出，电荷歧化及其伴随的极性位移可使层状极性金属 Sr₃Co₂O₇ 获得巨大的磁晶各向异性。研究将这一效应归因于钴局域晶场的重构，使面内磁化时轨道角动量得以恢复。
papers.method_en: The study uses first-principles calculations to compare magnetization directions and examine the role of charge disproportionation and polar displacements. Local Green-function and orbital-moment analyses are used to connect the anisotropy to orbital response, while the conventional second-order contribution is assessed within the adopted approximation.
papers.method_zh: 研究采用第一性原理计算比较不同磁化方向，并考察电荷歧化和极性位移的作用。作者通过局域格林函数和轨道磁矩分析将各向异性与轨道响应联系起来，同时在所采用的近似下评估传统二阶贡献。

papers.abstract: The gyroid, a triply periodic minimal surface found widely in nature and materials, has remained largely unexplored as a design principle for magnetic order. We introduce gyroidal magnetic order on the hyperoctagon lattice, the skeletal network of the gyroid, in which each magnetic moment points along the local $C_3$ axis that coincides with the local normal to the gyroid surface. The resulting noncoplanar spin texture constitutes a direct magnetic imprint of the gyroid geometry. We show that this order can be stabilized by single-ion anisotropy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, or the symmetric off-diagonal $Γ$ interaction combined with the Kitaev interaction, and remains robust against quantum fluctuations. Its magnon spectrum hosts symmetry-enforced pseudospin-1 and pseudospin-1/2 Weyl points that, unlike their electronic counterparts, persist under symmetry-allowed perturbations. Our results establish the gyroid as a geometric platform for magnetic order and symmetry-enforced topological magnon excitations.

papers.abstract: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.

papers.abstract: Electrides and altermagnets are two distinct yet intriguing classes of quantum materials, characterized by interstitial anionic electrons and nonrelativistic spin splitting, respectively. The recent prediction of Stoner-instability-driven altermagnetic electride provides a natural bridge between these two fields. Here, we investigate the magnetoelectric response and its related spin-polarized transport in the altermagnetic electride Zr$_2$N monolayer. Using the tight-binding Hubbard model and first-principles calculations, we find that the electric field can break the magnetic compensation between the two interstitial anionic electrons, inducing a finite net magnetization and giving rise to an interstitial electron mediated magnetoelectric response. papers.abstract: Correlated quantum phenomena arising from spin-orbit-coupled degrees of freedom provide foundational paradigms in emerging quantum technologies and spin-based functionalities. Elucidating the cooperative behaviors of these systems requires a precise probing of their intertwined magnetic and structural configurations. Using complementary resonant X-ray diffraction and high-energy total scattering measurements on single crystals of Sr2IrO4, we observe that spontaneous structural distortions scale quadratically with the magnetic order parameter. papers.abstract: Quantum geometric effects such as the Berry curvature and the quantum metric are well established in electronic transport, whereas in lattice dynamics the Berry curvature also plays a key role: adiabatically following the lattice, electrons generate a molecular Berry curvature that splits degenerate optical phonons into chiral partners. To determine how the quantum metric affects phonons, we go beyond adiabatic lattice dynamics, identifying Berry curvature and quantum metric contributions to the electronic response of the lattice. Using first-principles calculations in the magnetic topological semimetal EuB$_6$, we find that phonon modes with chiral splitting and those with nonchiral splitting coexist. Unlike the former, which originate from the Berry curvature, the latter arise from the pure quantum metric, while the Berry curvature contribution is forbidden by crystal symmetry.

papers.abstract: In antiferromagnets, the handedness of magnon precession is usually measured on single crystals. In a pressed pellet of the chiral helimagnet CsCuCl$_3$, whose grains carry both structural handednesses and all orientations, we found that, from 5 to 7 T, the sub-terahertz magnon absorbs one circular polarization more than 20 times as strongly as the other, which rules out precession about each grain's own axis. Magnon chirality in antiferromagnets is thus accessible without a single crystal.

papers.abstract: Recent studies have revealed the profound influence of Berry curvature on electron crystallization, yet the independent role of the quantum metric remains unclear. Here, we introduce a minimal three-band continuum model with separately tunable quantum metric and Berry flux. Employing the Hartree-Fock approach, we find that a conventional s-wave Wigner crystal can develop a hollow charge distribution with depleted density at lattice sites, without a change in symmetry or topology. We show that this density reconstruction occurs even at vanishing Berry curvature and arises from strong quantum metric and the nontrivial angular structure of the form factor. papers.abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

papers.abstract: The emergence of coherent heavy quasiparticles in Kondo lattices is generally accompanied by a reduction in electrical resistivity at low temperatures. However, certain strongly correlated metals exhibit anomalously large resistivities that persist to very low temperatures, raising fundamental questions about the mechanisms governing charge transport. Here, we report an unusual magnetic field-induced evolution of electronic transport and thermodynamic properties in a Ce-based heavy fermion compound, Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$. At zero field, Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$ undergoes a magnetic transition at $T$$_{0}$ = 0.45 K and exhibits a strongly enhanced low temperature specific heat coefficient, reaching $C$/$T$ = 2.2 J/mol$_{Ce}$-K$^{2}$, but no discernible coherence in its electrical resistivity. Remarkably, applying a magnetic field produces a large negative magnetoresistance and restores coherent metallic behavior, characterized by low-temperature $T$$^2$ resistivity. Although the field dependence of the electronic specific heat coefficient can be described phenomenologically within a single-ion Kondo framework, the same description fails to account for the strong suppression of the residual resistivity and the overall magnetoresistance. These results point to an additional field-sensitive scattering contribution beyond conventional single-ion Kondo physics. The striking resemblance to the long-standing anomalous magnetotransport behavior of UBe$_{13}$, without the complications introduced by superconductivity, establishes Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$ as a platform for investigating the microscopic origin of anomalous scattering and field-induced coherent transport in strongly correlated electron systems.

papers.abstract: The origin of superconductivity near 30~K in Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$BiO$_3$ has remained a long-standing puzzle. Tunneling experiments give an electron--boson coupling $λ\approx 0.7$--1.2, whereas density-functional calculations give $λ\approx 0.3$, concentrated in the breathing mode near 50--70~meV. We propose that the missing coupling of about 0.7 comes from dynamical charge fluctuations at Q=(pi,pi,pi)/a, the ordering vector of the charge-disproportionated parent compound, and introduce an overdamped boson model to describe them. Using a tight-binding fit to the conduction band found from density-functional calculations at $x=0.4$, we show that such a boson scatters electrons strongly only on hot lines of the Fermi surface, small loops around the $\langle 111\rangle$ directions where k and k+Q are both at the Fermi level. We derive closed-form self-energies, quasiparticle residues and band reconstructions, including shadow bands and hot-line pseudogaps for long-range correlations, and show that a sum rule fixes the Fermi-surface-averaged coupling independently of the boson frequency and correlation length. Combining the LDA phonon with an overdamped mode of frequency $ω_m\approx 25$~meV and coupling $λ\approx 0.7$, anisotropic Eliashberg calculations reproduce $T_c\approx 25$--30~K for correlation lengths of two to three lattice spacings and predict a gap enhanced by a factor of 3--4 on the hot loops. For longer correlation lengths an $s$-wave state competes closely with a sign-changing $T_{2g}$ state confined to the hot loops. In the random-phase approximation for an extended Hubbard model, the boson emerges naturally near a charge instability at $R$, but purely electronic fluctuations are too weak and too long-ranged; coupling to the breathing-mode lattice distortion is one possible way to strengthen them.

papers.abstract: Superconducting vortex represents a topological entity in type-II superconductors, where the prototypical manifestation of such a macroscopic quantum state holds great promise for applications in future quantum technologies. Deterministic control of the vortex dynamics at the nanoscale is central to enhance superconductors' critical thresholds and design next-generation superconducting quantum devices. However, it is still scientifically challenging due to the intrinsic nature of the vortex pinning landscapes in superconductors. Here, we observe an even-in-field Hall-like signal with about two order of magnitude enhancement in a type-II superconductor/chiral magnet heterostructure, which confines to the field-temperature window where the flux flow coexists with magnetic skyrmions. The polarity of such a giant even-in-field transverse response reverses between orthogonal current directions, suggesting an on-track vortex flow driven by a nematic fluxon-skyrmion interaction analyzed via the extended vortex-viscosity tensor. More critically, a deterministic manipulation of skyrmions at the nanoscale within the hybrid system enables selective and reversible controls over the dissipative behavior and therefore the reconfigurable fluxon transport, mimic the precise control of curling stone in winter Olympic, thereby opening a new avenue towards the exploration of programmable topological and superconducting quantum devices.

papers.abstract: Spin resonance modes are among the most characteristic collective excitations of unconventional superconductors, yet their microscopic origin remains unresolved. Although commonly interpreted as purely magnetic excitations, this picture does not explain the rich magnetic field evolution of these modes observed in heavy-fermion superconductors. Here we combine inelastic neutron scattering and symmetry analysis to investigate the evolution of the spin resonance modes in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeCoIn$_5$ under an in-plane magnetic field. papers.abstract: We investigate superconducting proximity effects in NbN/Pt/Py and NbN/Cu/Py trilayers using broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR). The reduction of the spin-pumping contribution to the Py damping below the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) is used to probe the superconducting correlations and electronic density of state in the buried metallic interlayer. For a Cu interlayer, the damping reduction remains finite up to at least 20 nm, in agreement with the large coherence length above 100nm in Cu. In contrast, the damping reduction for a Pt interlayer exhibits a non-monotonic thickness dependence and is fully suppressed above 5 nm. Using the quasiclassical theory, we are able to explain the oscillation in damping reduction below Tc with the coexistence of superconducting and magnetic proximity effects in Pt, which generates oscillations of the superconducting order parameter and electronic density of state in the exchange-splitted Pt interlayer. Our results establish spin-pumping damping as a sensitive probe of superconducting proximity effects in buried metallic layers.

papers.abstract: A flat band with a nonzero Chern number has no localized Wannier orbitals, which raises the question of whether Mott physics is still possible. We place a Hubbard interaction $U$ on coherent orbitals, which are localized but overcomplete, and develop a single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for this model. Within the flat band alone, DMFT reproduces the experimentally observed cascade and inverse-compressibility sawtooth without invoking Dirac revival or remote-band electrons. At nonzero integer filling we find an insulator-to-metal transition tuned by $s^2$, the fraction of the Brillouin zone that carries the Berry curvature. For $N_f=8$ flavors the Mott transition at $ν=-2$ occurs at $s^2_c\approx0.025$, where the top of the lower Hubbard band reaches the Fermi level and the local moments are Kondo screened, forming a heavy Fermi liquid (HFL). The HFL extends to the hole-doped side, $ν=-2-x$, but above the small Kondo temperature $T_K$ the state is an incoherent bad metal without a Fermi surface. At low temperature, an anti-Hund's coupling $J_A\sim0.1U$ replaces the HFL with a pseudogap metal that has a small Fermi surface and is dominated by spin-polaron excitations at small $x$. We propose this pseudogap metal as the parent state of superconductivity in TBG. The framework may also be applied to other topological bands, such as those of twisted WSe$_2$.

papers.abstract: The low-energy electronic structure of ABA trilayer graphene is composed of light and heavy electron branches, which can be altered by an out-of-plane displacement field. Here, we show that, depending on the values of Slonczewski-Weiss-McClure parameters, a displacement field can inflict a band edge inversion, for which we identify the inversion conditions. This inversion is accompanied by a reversal of Berry curvature and giant topological magnetic moments at the band edges. In a weak perpendicular magnetic field, those topological magnetic moments produce valley splitting, giving rise to distinct anomalous transverse electrical and thermoelectric responses. papers.abstract: Noncontacting light control of ferroelectric (FE) order has been receiving extensive interest in condensed matter physics. In this work, we investigate near-resonant light irradiation that induces structure-dependent photoexcited carrier density along the transition pathway. We combine a minimal Rice-Mele model containing intersite density-density correlations with ab initio calculations for realistic materials such as GeTe and SnTe. If the photon energy is below-gap without carrier excitation, only off-resonant scattering occurs and the FE order tends to be diminished. Slightly increasing photon energy at the near-gap regime would lead to a centrosymmetric non-polar (NP) to FE phase transition, which is not thermally accessible in conventional pressure-temperature phase diagram. This is in contrast to the well-above-gap light situation that tends to suppress the FE order under a fixed amount of photoexcitation. We apply phenomenological Landau theory and show that they belong to the continuous and first-order phase transitions, respectively. The occupation constrained calculations suggest that these reversible NP-FE phase transitions could be triggered under moderate light fluence. Our mechanism provides a potential route to reversible light-stabilized polar phases with reduced lattice heating and marginal lattice damages.

papers.abstract: Unlike fractional quantum Hall states in uniform Landau levels, fractional Chern insulators can host dispersive anyon bands, raising the question of what happens when the anyon gap closes. We construct an exact finite-bond-dimension tensor-network state for a fractional Chern semimetal by Gutzwiller projecting a critical parton state. This state exhibits divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors but a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of $1/3$. Although it has one electron per unit cell, its modular $S$ and $T$ matrices and entanglement spectrum match those of the $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state. We identify a $(1+1)$--dimensional $U(3)_1\times SU(3)_1$ conformal field theory (CFT) governing the wavefunction norm in the infrared, an unexpected result for a state with $U(1)_3$ topology. The $SU(3)_1$ sector is a nonlinear sigma model whose Wess--Zumino level and kinetic stiffness are determined by the parton Chern number and Fubini--Study metric, respectively. Under renormalization, it flows to the conformal fixed point, with an initial distance to this fixed point controlled by the idealness of parton quantum geometry. Favorable geometry enables precise agreement with CFT predictions even on narrow cylinders.

papers.result_en: The state has divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors, a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of 1/3, and modular S and T matrices and an entanglement spectrum matching those of the ν=1/3 Laughlin state despite having one electron per unit cell. papers.future_en: Further work could examine the proposed geometry-dependent conformal behavior across other parton constructions and determine how robust the CFT agreement is beyond the favorable-geometry and narrow-cylinder regimes described here.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可在其他部分子构造中考察所提出的几何依赖共形行为，并确定在此处所述的理想几何和窄圆柱条件之外，共形场论的一致性是否仍然稳健。

papers.abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$Ω$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. Local indentation with a $\sim$1 $μ$m-apex-radius needle reconfigures these domains, producing write/erase-like changes in wedge-shaped regions. These results establish local mechanical-field domain engineering in a relatively conducting CDW semiconductor, with possible contributions from both ferroelastic-like and flexoelectric mechanisms.
papers.physics_advance: Local indentation reconfigures the approximately 90-degree in-plane polar domains in EuTe4 at room temperature, with ferroelastic-like and flexoelectric contributions proposed.
papers.relevance_reason: The experiments establish mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in a conducting charge-density-wave semiconductor, a material phenomenon beyond a device-performance result.

papers.method_en: The authors use polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements to characterize the in-plane polarization domains, then apply a local indentation with a needle of approximately 1 μm apex radius.
papers.method_zh: 作者利用偏振光显微镜和二次谐波测量表征面内极化畴，随后使用尖端半径约为 1 μm 的针进行局部压痕。

Local indentation reconfigures the domains and produces write/erase-like changes in wedge-shaped regions at room temperature. The authors suggest that ferroelastic-like and flexoelectric mechanisms may both contribute.

The demonstrated write/erase-like response also motivates testing how reproducibly local mechanical actuation controls domains in this conducting CDW material.

papers.abstract: Many emerging solid-state platforms for Floquet engineering, nonlinear transport, and high harmonic generation operate near the Keldysh crossover, where optical fields are sufficiently strong and fast to reshape electronic states on sub-cycle timescales. Despite its importance, the microscopic pathways for photocarrier generation in this regime remain poorly understood, as neither perturbative multiphoton absorption nor adiabatic tunneling provides an adequate description. Here, we perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS$_3$ while systematically tuning the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. In the crossover regime, we observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel - a clear spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Hubbard-model simulations based on a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach qualitatively reproduce these features. Together, our results elucidate the microscopic mechanisms of charge excitation in the Keldysh crossover regime and identify a key ingredient for controlling strong-field nonlinear dynamics in correlated materials.
papers.physics_advance: In NiPS₃, the Keldysh crossover features ponderomotively blue-shifted multiphoton-like resonances within tunneling-dominated absorption, providing a spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown.
papers.relevance_reason: This combines spectroscopy and correlated-electron modeling to identify a new strong-field charge-excitation mechanism in a correlated quantum material.
papers.summary_zh: 本研究考察关联范德华绝缘体 NiPS₃ 在 Keldysh 交叉区附近的强场光生载流子产生，此时微扰多光子吸收或绝热隧穿均不足以单独描述过程。作者报告了隧穿主导吸收通道中绝热性失效的光谱证据。
papers.method_en: The authors perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on NiPS₃ while varying the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. They compare the observations with Hubbard-model simulations using a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach.
papers.method_zh: 作者对 NiPS₃ 进行时间分辨光学光谱测量，并在较宽范围内改变驱动电场和频率。他们将实验观测与采用时间依赖高斯变分方法的 Hubbard 模型模拟进行比较。
papers.result_en: In the Keldysh crossover regime, the authors observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects. These features occur within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel and are identified as a spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Time-dependent Gaussian variational simulations qualitatively reproduce the observed features. The results clarify photocarrier excitation in this crossover regime and identify a consideration relevant to controlling strong-field nonlinear dynamics in correlated materials.
papers.result_zh: 在 Keldysh 交叉区，作者观测到呈多光子特征的共振，其蓝移归因于有质动力效应。这些特征出现在总体由隧穿主导的吸收通道中，并被识别为绝热性失效的光谱标志。时间依赖高斯变分模拟在定性上再现了实验特征。结果阐明了该交叉区中的光生载流子激发，并指出了控制关联材料强场非线性动力学时需要考虑的因素。
papers.future_en: Further studies could test whether the observed ponderomotive blue shifts and multiphoton-like resonances persist across the drive-field and frequency ranges relevant to the Keldysh crossover. Improving the microscopic description beyond the reported qualitative agreement would also help assess the proposed excitation picture.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可检验观测到的有质动力蓝移和多光子型共振是否在 Keldysh 交叉区相关的驱动电场与频率范围内持续存在。进一步改进微观描述、超越摘要所述的定性吻合，也有助于评估所提出的激发图像。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract reports a clear spectroscopic signature of nonadiabaticity in the Keldysh crossover, supported by qualitative Hubbard-model simulations, and addresses a timely strong-field problem in correlated materials. The reported advance appears conceptually focused and significant, supporting a PRL-level assessment rather than a broader top-tier claim on the abstract alone.
